projects.name: TravelTide Analytics Engine (Core Module)
projects.description: The analytical engine of the TravelTide project: a modular Python package handling data ingestion (CSV/SQL/DB), EDA, feature engineering (PCA, clustering, normalization), ML-based segmentation (KMeans, DBSCAN), perk assignment, and non-ML segment reporting — designed for scalability and reusability.
business_insights: A single modular pipeline (utils → load_data → eda → advance_metrics → perk_assignment → segment_analyse) makes customer segmentation and perk personalization reproducible end-to-end
Separating ML-based clustering from non-ML segment analysis lets business stakeholders validate findings through two independent lenses
Centralized data loading with auto-caching to CSV keeps repeated DB queries fast and consistent across notebooks

key_metrics.pipeline_stages: Load → EDA → Feature Engineering → ML Segmentation → Perk Assignment → Reporting

suggested_visualizations: Flowchart of the 6-module architecture (utils → load_data → eda → advance_metrics → perk_assignment → segment_analyse)
2D/3D PCA scatter plots colored by cluster assignment
Perk-assignment matrix mapping clusters to scored perks
Correlation heatmap from correlation_analysis()
Segment comparison bar charts from segment_analyse.py
technical_details_missing: Feature standardization via StandardScaler prior to KMeans/DBSCAN
PCA feature importance ranking used to interpret cluster drivers
Cluster profiling step before perk scoring to ensure business relevance
Auto-caching of DB query results to CSV to avoid redundant queries
Runner script (run_pipeline.py) to automate the full workflow end-to-end
sql_insights: Built a PostgreSQL connection layer (get_db_connection) with reusable SQL execution helpers (execute_sql, execute_sql_file)
Centralized SQL/CSV/DB loading through a single load_table() interface
Implemented datetime conversion and duration-calculation utilities for time-based SQL fields
ai_insights: Implemented KMeans and DBSCAN clustering for behavioral segmentation
Used PCA for dimensionality reduction and feature importance analysis
Built a perk-scoring and unique perk-assignment system on top of cluster profiles

projects.name: User Session Analytics Pipeline (SQL CTE Architecture)
projects.description: A production-grade SQL pipeline built with Common Table Expressions that filters sessions to a defined time window, identifies high-engagement users (>7 sessions), and enriches them with demographic, flight, and hotel data into a single analytical dataset for BI, churn modeling, and segmentation.
business_insights: Users with more than 7 sessions are disproportionately likely to book flights, add hotels, and use discounts
The unified dataset enables discount-elasticity and promotion-effectiveness analysis despite sparse discount-amount fields
Home airport, family status, and age correlate with trip distance, hotel nights, and airline choice, supporting demographic-driven personalization
suggested_visualizations: Pipeline architecture diagram: sessions_2023 → filtered_users → session_base → final SELECT
Funnel chart from raw sessions to high-engagement, enriched sessions
Bar chart comparing booking rates for high-engagement vs. all users
Left-join enrichment diagram showing user/flight/hotel attribute additions
technical_details_missing: CTE 1 (sessions_2023) pre-filters by date to improve downstream join performance
CTE 2 (filtered_users) aggregates session counts per user before applying the HAVING threshold
CTE 3 (session_base) performs left joins to preserve session-level granularity
Attributes enriched: birthdate, gender, marital status, children, home airport (lat/lon), sign-up date, flight itinerary, hotel stay details
sql_insights: Used a 3-stage CTE architecture for readability, maintainability, and production-readiness
Applied time-window filtering to restrict analysis to relevant, recent behavior
Used LEFT JOINs to preserve session-level rows even when flight/hotel data is absent

projects.name: TravelTide Data Loading & Quality Assessment
projects.description: The foundational data-loading and quality-assessment layer for the TravelTide pipeline. Loads raw data from CSV/SQL sources, runs missing-value diagnostics across all tables, and produces the enriched base_sessions dataset used for all downstream analysis.
business_insights: The users table is 100% complete across all 11 demographic columns, enabling confident user-level personalization
Only 43.19% of sessions have a trip_id, revealing significant window-shopping behavior worth retargeting
83–87% missing discount-amount fields suggest binary discount indicators are more reliable than raw amounts for elasticity modeling
suggested_visualizations: Entity-relationship diagram: users → sessions → flights/hotels → base_sessions
Missing-value heatmap across the four source tables
Distribution plots for page_clicks, base_fare_usd, and nights
Bar chart of round-trip (95.3%) vs. one-way flight bookings
technical_details_missing: base_sessions is derived by filtering sessions after Jan 4, 2023 and keeping users with >7 sessions
SQL execution results are auto-cached to /data/processed/session_base.csv
Negative values found in the nights column flagged for validation-rule improvements
Numerical summary statistics (mean, quartiles, std) computed for all key booking features
sql_insights: Executed the CTE-based session_base SQL query to construct the enriched base_sessions dataset
Used execute_sql/load_table utilities to load raw and processed tables interchangeably
